global_style.style_reference: Illustrated Parish Notebook concept art only. Definitive surface split: the actual world/scene layer is the painted watercolor surface; UI portraits, notebook tabs, notes, icons, and other UI furniture are uncolored pen-and-ink line art on paper with minimal value shading. In-world NPC markers may use restrained watercolor because they live on the painted world surface. Do not use prior experimental portrait sheets, marker concept sheets, procedural busts, or unrelated graphics cycles as authority.

portrait_source: portrait line art occupies roughly 45 percent of source height
centered head-and-shoulders drawing with generous transparent padding on all sides
top of hair/head covering and shoulders fully visible
no baked parchment, paper texture, wash, card, border, label, or UI furniture
marker_source: full-body figure occupies roughly 45 percent of source height
centered figure with feet fully visible and generous flat background margins
one single static in-world marker pose per NPC for this slice
no ground shadow, floor plane, label, border, or extra figure
runtime_derivatives: approved portrait sources are converted to transparent PNGs and composited over UI-controlled parchment
selected-person portrait target is approximately 99x112 px on desktop and 58x66 px on mobile
nearby-rail portrait target is approximately 51x57 px on desktop and 36x41 px on mobile
approved marker sources are chroma-keyed to transparent PNGs and depth-scaled by the notebook renderer
sheet_policy: do not require a per-character animation sprite sheet for the current marker slice
pack approved static runtime portraits and markers into a shared runtime atlas only after review if renderer performance needs it
add per-NPC pose or facing sheets only when gameplay explicitly needs animated movement, directional facing, or state-specific work poses

medium: sepia or graphite linework with minimal value shading for UI art
transparent portrait line art composited over UI-controlled paper
paper-native texture supplied by the UI, not baked into portrait art
palette: concept palette anchor: olive-grey and weathered tan #6e634e, #807661, #9e8e75, #b5a285
UI portraits: transparent background plus sepia or graphite ink only
UI portraits: no colored wash or color fill
UI portraits: minimal monochrome value shading only
world/marker art: restrained watercolor only where the asset sits in the painted world
world/marker art: muted wool grey, bog green, dull brick red, peat brown, faded indigo only as subordinate accents
avoid saturated primaries; #ff00ff is allowed only as marker chroma key
common_constraints: identity-specific named NPC, not a generic color variant
readable at Nearby rail portrait size and tiny in-scene marker size
NPC UI portraits must be uncolored pen-and-ink line art with minimal shading; no colored wash, no color fill, no painted clothing blocks
NPC UI portraits must be transparent-background assets so the notebook UI controls the paper surface
no Victorian bustle, top hat, bowler, police uniform, photography-era styling, fantasy costume, weapon focus, text, labels, icons, decorative border, watermark, or abstract placeholder bust
show dignity, warmth, and specificity without caricature

portrait_identity.face_and_hair: plain parish-neighbour face, hair mostly hidden by a soft cap or simple shawl, no strong likeness cues
portrait_identity.clothing: plain homespun outer layer, linen at the neck, muted cap or shawl
portrait_identity.pose_expression: neutral, approachable, unspecific
props: none, or one indistinct small bundle
palette_notes: describe clothing with ink texture and line weight only
use paper tone plus sepia/graphite value

marker_identity.silhouette: ordinary villager silhouette with cap or shawl and no distinctive trade prop
marker_identity.pose: small standing figure, slightly turned, hands near body
tiny_readability_notes: must read as a production villager, but must not be confusable with any named NPC
avoid strong age, occupation, or family cues

authoring_notes: Fallback exists only for NPCs without approved art at runtime; named NPCs still require their own art direction.

portrait_identity.face_and_hair: weathered broad face, heavy brows, greying sideburns, short rough beard shadow or trimmed grey whiskers
portrait_identity.clothing: rolled linen sleeves, dark worn waistcoat, plain neckcloth, publican's apron hinted low in frame
portrait_identity.pose_expression: gruff but warm, looking up from work as if ready with dry advice

marker_identity.silhouette: stocky older publican with squared shoulders and waistcoat
marker_identity.pose: one hand at bar-rag or cup, grounded behind-the-bar stance
tiny_readability_notes: stocky shape plus cup/rag should distinguish him from other older men
do not rely on facial detail alone

authoring_notes: Canonical data gives age, publican role, pub location, and behind-the-bar cue, but not stable hair, clothing, or marker silhouette.

portrait_identity.face_and_hair: sun-browned practical face, steady eyes, hair tucked under a dark kerchief
portrait_identity.clothing: plain wool dress or bodice, sturdy apron, muddy hem, work shawl pinned tight
portrait_identity.pose_expression: determined and no-nonsense, slightly forward posture

marker_identity.silhouette: sturdy farm woman with kerchief, apron, and broad practical stance
marker_identity.pose: standing with one hand on hip and one near a pail or farm tool
tiny_readability_notes: kerchief and pail must read at rail size
avoid making her only a generic middle-aged woman

authoring_notes: Canonical data is weak visually: it says middle-aged farmer, schedules and farm context add work cues, but appearance needs supplement.
